preamble: A coda /t/ takes on the bilabial place of a following /p/, /b/ or /m/, giving [p] (regressive place assimilation). The process is asymmetric: coronals assimilate to labials and velars, while labials and velars rarely assimilate to coronals. In Sino-Japanese compounds the original coda /t/ of borrowed Middle Chinese morphemes became fully assimilated to a following /p/, giving geminate [pp] as in shuppatsu and shippai.

examples.note: Coda /t/ of a Sino-Japanese morpheme (from Middle Chinese -t) does not take its epenthetic vowel before a voiceless obstruent and is realized as the geminate mora /Q/, copying the place of the following /p/.
Same assimilation; 一 ichi + 杯 hai gives 一杯 ippai 'one cup, full'.
